contextBoundaryNote: Edexcel Option 31 strictly examines 1918 to August 1939 before the Second World War; wartime resistance, euthanasia, and extermination programmes fall outside this specification.

root.label: Weimar & Nazi Germany
root.gloss: Germany from First World War defeat and Weimar democracy in 1918 through Hitler's rise to a totalitarian Nazi dictatorship by August 1939.

children.label: KT1: The Weimar Republic
children.gloss: Key topic 1: The Weimar Republic, 1918–29 — origins amid war collapse, early 1919–23 crises, Stresemann's recovery, and Weimar social and cultural change.

children.label: 1.1 Origins of the Republic
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: View 1 argues the Republic was crippled from birth by armistice shame and Article 48 flaws vs View 2 argues Ebert and progressive democratic rights saved Germany from chaos.

children.label: Unrest, Abdication & Armistice
children.gloss: Situation in Germany at the end of the War brought political unrest, the abdication of the Kaiser, the November armistice, and a new republic.

children.label: Allied Blockade & Kiel Mutiny
children.detail: Severe food shortages killed 750,000 civilians and sparked 40,000 sailors at Kiel to revolt against imperial rule.
children.gloss: Severe food shortages killed 750,000 civilians and sparked 40,000 sailors at Kiel to revolt against imperial rule.

children.label: Wilhelm II Fled to Holland
children.detail: Losing army loyalty at Spa on 9 November 1918, the Kaiser abdicated as Scheidemann proclaimed a democratic state.
children.gloss: Losing army loyalty at Spa on 9 November 1918, the Kaiser abdicated as Scheidemann proclaimed a democratic state.

children.label: November Armistice Tainted Ebert
children.detail: Erzberger signing surrender on 11 November let nationalists brand civilian democrats traitors from day one.
children.gloss: Erzberger signing surrender on 11 November let nationalists brand civilian democrats traitors from day one.

children.label: Ebert-Groener Pact Averted Chaos
children.detail: Securing Imperial Army backing and civil service continuity prevented an immediate Bolshevik-style civil war.
children.gloss: Securing Imperial Army backing and civil service continuity prevented an immediate Bolshevik-style civil war.

children.label: Weimar Constitution Design
children.gloss: The new Weimar Constitution combined progressive democratic strengths in Germany with dangerous structural weaknesses.

children.label: National Assembly Met in Weimar
children.detail: Violent street fighting in Berlin forced elected deputies in February 1919 to draft laws in a peaceful town.
children.gloss: Violent street fighting in Berlin forced elected deputies in February 1919 to draft laws in a peaceful town.

children.label: 83% Turnout Backed Moderate Rule
children.detail: Social Democrats, Centre, and Democratic parties won over three-quarters of seats in the January 1919 vote.
children.gloss: Social Democrats, Centre, and Democratic parties won over three-quarters of seats in the January 1919 vote.

children.label: PR & Article 48 Weakened Rule
children.detail: Proportional representation splintered 29 parties while presidential emergency decrees bypassed Parliament.
children.gloss: Proportional representation splintered 29 parties while presidential emergency decrees bypassed Parliament.

children.label: Universal Vote at Age Twenty
children.detail: Equal male and female suffrage, free speech, and elected seven-year presidents built modern European liberty.
children.gloss: Equal male and female suffrage, free speech, and elected seven-year presidents built modern European liberty.

children.label: 1.2 Early Weimar Challenges
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: View 1 argues the Treaty of Versailles and 1923 Ruhr hyperinflation dealt the Republic its worst blow vs View 2 argues armed Left and Right revolts posed the deadlier danger.

children.label: Versailles & Stab in the Back
children.gloss: Early unpopularity of the Republic stemmed from the stab in the back theory and harsh key terms of the Treaty of Versailles.

children.label: Allied Diktat Forced Signature
children.detail: Threatened with renewed Allied invasion, civilian ministers had no choice but to sign peace on 28 June 1919.
children.gloss: Threatened with renewed Allied invasion, civilian ministers had no choice but to sign peace on 28 June 1919.

children.label: Article 231 & £6.6bn Reparations
children.detail: War guilt, a 100,000-man army cap, zero submarines or planes, and losing 13% of territory enraged voters.
children.gloss: War guilt, a 100,000-man army cap, zero submarines or planes, and losing 13% of territory enraged voters.

children.label: Dolchstoss Poisoned Legitimacy
children.detail: Hindenburg's myth that undefeated soldiers were betrayed at home permanently alienated nationalist voters.
children.gloss: Hindenburg's myth that undefeated soldiers were betrayed at home permanently alienated nationalist voters.

children.label: Peace Preserved National Unity
children.detail: Accepting harsh Allied terms prevented foreign dismemberment and gave German democracy breathing space.
children.gloss: Accepting harsh Allied terms prevented foreign dismemberment and gave German democracy breathing space.

children.label: Spartacists, Freikorps & Kapp
children.gloss: Violent challenges to the Republic from Left and Right included the Spartacists, the Freikorps, and the 1920 Kapp Putsch.

children.label: Extremists Rejected Democracy
children.detail: Communists wanted Soviet councils while nationalist ex-soldiers despised Versailles military cuts.
children.gloss: Communists wanted Soviet councils while nationalist ex-soldiers despised Versailles military cuts.

children.label: 376 Political Murders by 1922
children.detail: Right-wing Organisation Consul gunmen assassinated Erzberger and Foreign Minister Walther Rathenau.
children.gloss: Right-wing Organisation Consul gunmen assassinated Erzberger and Foreign Minister Walther Rathenau.

children.label: Workers Defeated the Kapp Coup
children.detail: When Reichswehr generals refused to shoot Freikorps rebels in March 1920, a Berlin general strike saved Ebert.
children.gloss: When Reichswehr generals refused to shoot Freikorps rebels in March 1920, a Berlin general strike saved Ebert.

children.label: Army & Judges Backed the Right
children.detail: Crushing Luxemburg and Liebknecht brutally while sparing right-wing putschists exposed deadly elite bias.
children.gloss: Crushing Luxemburg and Liebknecht brutally while sparing right-wing putschists exposed deadly elite bias.

children.label: Ruhr Crisis & Hyperinflation
children.gloss: Challenges of 1923 centred on hyperinflation alongside the reasons for and effects of the French occupation of the Ruhr.

children.label: Missed Coal Debt Sparked Invasion
children.detail: Defaulting on reparations brought 60,000 French and Belgian troops into Germany's industrial heartland.
children.gloss: Defaulting on reparations brought 60,000 French and Belgian troops into Germany's industrial heartland.

children.label: Printing Money for Passive Strike
children.detail: Paying striking Ruhr miners while collecting zero tax revenue collapsed the mark to 200 billion per loaf.
children.gloss: Paying striking Ruhr miners while collecting zero tax revenue collapsed the mark to 200 billion per loaf.

children.label: Middle-Class Savers Lost Everything
children.detail: Wiping out lifetime bank savings and fixed pensions turned respectable burger families against Weimar.
children.gloss: Wiping out lifetime bank savings and fixed pensions turned respectable burger families against Weimar.

children.label: Debtors Gained & Republic Survived
children.detail: Big industrialists cleared loans cheaply and Stresemann swiftly restored order without regime collapse.
children.gloss: Big industrialists cleared loans cheaply and Stresemann swiftly restored order without regime collapse.

children.label: 1.3 Recovery of the Republic
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: View 1 argues Stresemann achieved genuine economic recovery and international acceptance vs View 2 argues Weimar stability stayed a fragile volcano built on short-term US loans.

children.label: Stresemann & the Rentenmark
children.gloss: Economic recovery began when Gustav Stresemann ended passive resistance and stabilized currency with the new Rentenmark.

children.label: Halted Ruhr Strike & Burnt Notes
children.detail: Ending costly passive resistance in September 1923 stopped runaway money printing and reopened factories.
children.gloss: Ending costly passive resistance in September 1923 stopped runaway money printing and reopened factories.

children.label: Land-Backed Reichsmark in 1924
children.detail: Tying currency strictly to agricultural land and industrial mortgages restored shopkeeper trust overnight.
children.gloss: Tying currency strictly to agricultural land and industrial mortgages restored shopkeeper trust overnight.

children.label: Restored Confidence & Moderate Votes
children.detail: Sound currency revived domestic trade and boosted pro-Weimar coalitions in the December 1924 election.
children.gloss: Sound currency revived domestic trade and boosted pro-Weimar coalitions in the December 1924 election.

children.label: 1923 Savers Never Fully Repaid
children.detail: Refusing full compensation left ruined middle-class pensioners permanently bitter towards republican leaders.
children.gloss: Refusing full compensation left ruined middle-class pensioners permanently bitter towards republican leaders.

children.label: Dawes, Young & American Loans
children.gloss: The Dawes and Young Plans restructured reparations while American loans and investment funded Weimar economic recovery.

children.label: 800m Gold Marks Kickstarted Output
children.detail: Dawes in 1924 scaled annual payments to capacity, ended Ruhr occupation, and doubled industrial output by 1928.
children.gloss: Dawes in 1924 scaled annual payments to capacity, ended Ruhr occupation, and doubled industrial output by 1928.

children.label: Young Plan Cut Bill to £1.85bn
children.detail: Negotiated in 1929, the Young Plan slashed total reparations by three-quarters and extended payments to 1988.
children.gloss: Negotiated in 1929, the Young Plan slashed total reparations by three-quarters and extended payments to 1988.

children.label: Exports & Factories Surpassed 1913
children.detail: Over $2.5 billion in Wall Street capital modernised chemical, steel, and electrical plants across Germany.
children.gloss: Over $2.5 billion in Wall Street capital modernised chemical, steel, and electrical plants across Germany.

children.label: Dancing on a Short-Term Volcano
children.detail: Stresemann himself warned that prosperity relied on recallable US bank credit while farmers stayed in debt.
children.gloss: Stresemann himself warned that prosperity relied on recallable US bank credit while farmers stayed in debt.

children.label: Locarno Pact & League Entry
children.gloss: Stresemann gained international acceptance of Germany through the Locarno Pact and joining the League of Nations.

children.label: Fulfilment Diplomacy Built Trust
children.detail: Accepting western borders with France and Belgium voluntarily in 1925 ended Germany's postwar pariah status.
children.gloss: Accepting western borders with France and Belgium voluntarily in 1925 ended Germany's postwar pariah status.

children.label: Permanent League Council Seat 1926
children.detail: Germany entered the League as a great power, signed Kellogg-Briand in 1928, and won Allied Rhineland exit.
children.gloss: Germany entered the League as a great power, signed Kellogg-Briand in 1928, and won Allied Rhineland exit.

children.label: Peaceful Revision Won Allied Respect
children.detail: Stresemann won the 1926 Nobel Peace Prize and ended French threats of repeating the Ruhr occupation.
children.gloss: Stresemann won the 1926 Nobel Peace Prize and ended French threats of repeating the Ruhr occupation.

children.label: Right Attacked Treaty Appeasement
children.detail: Hugenberg and Hitler campaigned fiercely against Locarno and the Young Plan as cowardly betrayals of Germany.
children.gloss: Hugenberg and Hitler campaigned fiercely against Locarno and the Young Plan as cowardly betrayals of Germany.

children.label: 1.4 Weimar Society & Culture
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: View 1 argues 1924–29 delivered progressive Golden Years in living standards, female equality, and culture vs View 2 argues gains remained uneven and provoked fierce conservative backlash.

children.label: Wages, Homes & Living Standards
children.gloss: Changes in the standard of living brought rising industrial wages, council housing, and welfare insurance.

children.label: Real Wages Rose Over 25 Percent
children.detail: Strong trade union bargaining and Dawes investment lifted skilled urban workers to Europe's highest pay.
children.gloss: Strong trade union bargaining and Dawes investment lifted skilled urban workers to Europe's highest pay.

children.label: 1927 Unemployment Insurance Act
children.detail: Compulsory payroll contributions protected 17 million workers while councils built over two million homes.
children.gloss: Compulsory payroll contributions protected 17 million workers while councils built over two million homes.

children.label: Housing Shortage Cut by Two-Thirds
children.detail: Shorter eight-hour shifts, war veterans' pensions, and modern apartments transformed working-class security.
children.gloss: Shorter eight-hour shifts, war veterans' pensions, and modern apartments transformed working-class security.

children.label: Farmers & Clerks Faced Slump
children.detail: Global grain gluts bankrupted peasant smallholders by 1928 while white-collar unemployment stayed stubbornly high.
children.gloss: Global grain gluts bankrupted peasant smallholders by 1928 while white-collar unemployment stayed stubbornly high.

children.label: Women in Work, Politics & Leisure
children.gloss: Changes in the position of women transformed work, politics, and leisure for urban young Germans.

children.label: Equal Rights & White-Collar Jobs
children.detail: Article 109 granted equal civic rights while expanding department stores and offices hired female typists.
children.gloss: Article 109 granted equal civic rights while expanding department stores and offices hired female typists.

children.label: 112 Female Deputies Elected by 1933
children.detail: Around 90% of women voted, female doctors doubled, and bobbed-hair New Women smoked and went out unchaperoned.
children.gloss: Around 90% of women voted, female doctors doubled, and bobbed-hair New Women smoked and went out unchaperoned.

children.label: Broadest Female Freedom in Europe
children.detail: Financial independence in retail, teaching, and civil service broke rigid imperial patriarchal restrictions.
children.gloss: Financial independence in retail, teaching, and civil service broke rigid imperial patriarchal restrictions.

children.label: 33% Pay Gap & Double Burden
children.detail: Women earned a third less than men, zero sat in Cabinet, and churches condemned falling marriage birth rates.
children.gloss: Women earned a third less than men, zero sat in Cabinet, and churches condemned falling marriage birth rates.

children.label: Architecture, Art & Weimar Cinema
children.gloss: Cultural changes brought bold developments in Bauhaus architecture, New Objectivity art, and Expressionist cinema.

children.label: Ending Censorship Freed Creators
children.detail: Constitutional free expression let war-scarred artists question militarism, class greed, and authority.
children.gloss: Constitutional free expression let war-scarred artists question militarism, class greed, and authority.

children.label: Gropius, Otto Dix & Fritz Lang
children.detail: Steel-and-glass Bauhaus design, gritty war paintings, and UFA's Metropolis won worldwide artistic acclaim.
children.gloss: Steel-and-glass Bauhaus design, gritty war paintings, and UFA's Metropolis won worldwide artistic acclaim.

children.label: Berlin Led Global Modernist Culture
children.detail: Marlene Dietrich films, Brecht's theatre, and Remarque's anti-war novel thrilled millions of urban audiences.
children.gloss: Marlene Dietrich films, Brecht's theatre, and Remarque's anti-war novel thrilled millions of urban audiences.

children.label: Rural Voters Condemned Decadence
children.detail: Provincial conservatives and Nazis branded Berlin cabaret and avant-garde galleries un-German moral rot.
children.gloss: Provincial conservatives and Nazis branded Berlin cabaret and avant-garde galleries un-German moral rot.

children.label: KT2: Hitler's Rise to Power
children.gloss: Key topic 2: Hitler's rise to power, 1919–33 — founding the NSDAP and SA, the 1923 Munich Putsch and reorganisation, Great Depression surge, and January 1933 appointment.

children.label: 2.1 Early Nazi Party Growth
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: View 1 argues Hitler's spellbinding oratory and Führerprinzip leadership drove early NSDAP growth vs View 2 argues nationalist anger in the 25-Point Programme and SA brawling mattered more.

children.label: Hitler, DAP & Setting Up NSDAP
children.gloss: Hitler's early career moved from joining Anton Drexler's German Workers' Party in 1919 to setting up and leading the Nazi Party.

children.label: Army Spy Joined Drexler's Tiny DAP
children.detail: Sent to monitor Munich radicals in September 1919, Hitler shared their fierce anti-Versailles nationalism.
children.gloss: Sent to monitor Munich radicals in September 1919, Hitler shared their fierce anti-Versailles nationalism.

children.label: Swastika Branding & 1921 Takeover
children.detail: Designing the red-white-black banner and buying the Völkischer Beobachter helped grow membership past 3,000.
children.gloss: Designing the red-white-black banner and buying the Völkischer Beobachter helped grow membership past 3,000.

children.label: Oratory & Führerprinzip Built Unity
children.detail: Ousting Drexler in July 1921 gave Hitler sole command and packed Munich beer halls with 55,000 members by 1923.
children.gloss: Ousting Drexler in July 1921 gave Hitler sole command and packed Munich beer halls with 55,000 members by 1923.

children.label: Bavarian Right-Wing Climate Fed DAP
children.detail: Post-Soviet turmoil in Munich and sympathetic local elites sheltered dozens of similar nationalist leagues.
children.gloss: Post-Soviet turmoil in Munich and sympathetic local elites sheltered dozens of similar nationalist leagues.

children.label: 25-Point Programme & the SA
children.gloss: In 1920–21 the Twenty-Five Point Programme defined Nazi ideology while Ernst Röhm's SA policed streets and rallies.

children.label: Blended Nationalism & Worker Pledges
children.detail: Issued in February 1920, the platform demanded scrapping Versailles, Aryan citizenship, and profit-sharing.
children.gloss: Issued in February 1920, the platform demanded scrapping Versailles, Aryan citizenship, and profit-sharing.

children.label: Röhm Formed Brownshirt Stormtroopers
children.detail: Founded in August 1921 from jobless ex-Freikorps fighters, the SA guarded Nazi speakers and beat Communist rivals.
children.gloss: Founded in August 1921 from jobless ex-Freikorps fighters, the SA guarded Nazi speakers and beat Communist rivals.

children.label: Broad Manifesto Caught Angry Voters
children.detail: Attacking big department stores, treaties, and Jewish citizenship appealed simultaneously to clerks and workers.
children.gloss: Attacking big department stores, treaties, and Jewish citizenship appealed simultaneously to clerks and workers.

children.label: Rowdy SA Thugs Alienated Moderates
children.detail: Unruly street violence scared respectable middle-class voters and kept the NSDAP a regional Bavarian fringe.
children.gloss: Unruly street violence scared respectable middle-class voters and kept the NSDAP a regional Bavarian fringe.

children.label: 2.2 Munich Putsch & Lean Years
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: View 1 argues the 1923 Munich Putsch was a disastrous armed failure followed by 2.6% irrelevance vs View 2 argues trial fame, Mein Kampf, and Bamberg reorganisation forged future victory.

children.label: Munich Putsch Causes & Defeat
children.gloss: Hyperinflation, Stresemann ending Ruhr resistance, and Mussolini's Rome march triggered the failed 1923 Munich Putsch.

children.label: Ruhr Surrender & Impatient 50,000 SA
children.detail: Fearing Röhm's restless stormtroopers would desert once Stresemann called off strikes, Hitler gambled on force.
children.gloss: Fearing Röhm's restless stormtroopers would desert once Stresemann called off strikes, Hitler gambled on force.

children.label: Sixteen Nazis Shot in Munich Streets
children.detail: After Kahr and Lossow escaped and alerted Bavarian police, gunfire scattered 2,000 marchers and banned the NSDAP.
children.gloss: After Kahr and Lossow escaped and alerted Bavarian police, gunfire scattered 2,000 marchers and banned the NSDAP.

children.label: Amateur Planning Wrecked the Coup
children.detail: Failing to seize Munich's telegraph office or army barracks ended in Hitler's arrest and dislocated shoulder.
children.gloss: Failing to seize Munich's telegraph office or army barracks ended in Hitler's arrest and dislocated shoulder.

children.label: Taught Hitler Armed Force Would Fail
children.detail: Defeat proved power required winning Reichstag votes legally with army tolerance rather than fighting police.
children.gloss: Defeat proved power required winning Reichstag votes legally with army tolerance rather than fighting police.

children.label: Treason Trial & Mein Kampf
children.gloss: Long-term consequences of the Munich Putsch included nationwide trial publicity, lenient imprisonment, and Mein Kampf.

children.label: Right-Wing Judges Sympathised Openly
children.detail: Biased Munich judges let Hitler lecture reporters for 24 days before serving nine months in Landsberg Fortress.
children.gloss: Biased Munich judges let Hitler lecture reporters for 24 days before serving nine months in Landsberg Fortress.

children.label: Dictated Mein Kampf to Rudolf Hess
children.detail: Hitler's manifesto set out Aryan racial supremacy, Lebensraum in Eastern Europe, and destroying democracy.
children.gloss: Hitler's manifesto set out Aryan racial supremacy, Lebensraum in Eastern Europe, and destroying democracy.

children.label: Turned Hitler into a National Star
children.detail: Front-page newspaper coverage across Germany gave Hitler undisputed leadership of the extreme nationalist right.
children.gloss: Front-page newspaper coverage across Germany gave Hitler undisputed leadership of the extreme nationalist right.

children.label: Party Split While Hitler Was Jailed
children.detail: Without strong central command in 1924, rival northern and southern factions quarrelled and lost voters.
children.gloss: Without strong central command in 1924, rival northern and southern factions quarrelled and lost voters.

children.label: Lean Years & Bamberg Conference
children.gloss: Limited support for the Nazi Party in 1924–28 accompanied nationwide Party reorganisation and the Bamberg Conference of 1926.

children.label: Weimar Prosperity Starved Extremism
children.detail: Stable Rentenmark prices, rising wages, and Locarno diplomacy left voters little reason to back radical parties.
children.gloss: Stable Rentenmark prices, rising wages, and Locarno diplomacy left voters little reason to back radical parties.

children.label: 1926 Bamberg Beat Gregor Strasser
children.detail: Hitler crushed socialist land-reform demands, won over Goebbels, created 35 Gaue branches, and founded the SS.
children.gloss: Hitler crushed socialist land-reform demands, won over Goebbels, created 35 Gaue branches, and founded the SS.

children.label: Crushed to 12 Seats in May 1928
children.detail: Winning just 2.6% of the national vote despite 100,000 members showed propaganda failed during good times.
children.gloss: Winning just 2.6% of the national vote despite 100,000 members showed propaganda failed during good times.

children.label: National Machine Ready for Slump
children.detail: Gauleiters, Hitler Youth, and rural targeting built the exact organisational network that boomed after 1929.
children.gloss: Gauleiters, Hitler Youth, and rural targeting built the exact organisational network that boomed after 1929.

children.label: 2.3 Depression & Nazi Surge
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: View 1 argues Great Depression unemployment and fear of Communism drove voters to the Nazis vs View 2 argues Hitler's charisma, Goebbels' modern propaganda, and SA order won support.

children.label: Mass Unemployment & KPD Growth
children.gloss: The Wall Street Crash caused soaring unemployment and growing support for the Communist Party across industrial cities.

children.label: US Banks Recalled Short-Term Loans
children.detail: October 1929 Wall Street panic drained German factory credit, halving industrial production by winter 1932.
children.gloss: October 1929 Wall Street panic drained German factory credit, halving industrial production by winter 1932.

children.label: Brüning Cut Dole & Raised Taxes
children.detail: Ruling via 66 Article 48 decrees in 1932, the Hunger Chancellor deepened misery as joblessness hit six million.
children.gloss: Ruling via 66 Article 48 decrees in 1932, the Hunger Chancellor deepened misery as joblessness hit six million.

children.label: 100 KPD Seats Scared Middle Classes
children.detail: Rising Communist votes among desperate factory workers panicked farmers, shopkeepers, and industrial bosses.
children.gloss: Rising Communist votes among desperate factory workers panicked farmers, shopkeepers, and industrial bosses.

children.label: Slump Alone Did Not Pick the Winner
children.detail: Economic collapse discredited Weimar moderates, yet Goebbels still had to out-organise rival nationalist parties.
children.gloss: Economic collapse discredited Weimar moderates, yet Goebbels still had to out-organise rival nationalist parties.

children.label: Hitler's Appeal & Propaganda
children.gloss: Growth in support for the Nazi Party stemmed from the personal appeal of Hitler and the Nazis and Goebbels' propaganda.

children.label: Tailored Promises to Every Class
children.detail: Goebbels pledged Work and Bread to the jobless, debt relief to farmers, and anti-union order to businessmen.
children.gloss: Goebbels pledged Work and Bread to the jobless, debt relief to farmers, and anti-union order to businessmen.

children.label: Hitler Over Germany Flight Campaign
children.detail: Chartered planes, radio broadcasts, torchlit marches, and bold posters carried Hitler to twenty cities in days.
children.gloss: Chartered planes, radio broadcasts, torchlit marches, and bold posters carried Hitler to twenty cities in days.

children.label: Votes Only Exploded After 1929 Crash
children.detail: Jumping from 12 seats to 107 in 1930 and 230 in July 1932 mirrored rising unemployment almost line for line.
children.gloss: Jumping from 12 seats to 107 in 1930 and 230 in July 1932 mirrored rising unemployment almost line for line.

children.label: Strongman Image Inspired Mass Hope
children.detail: Thirteen million Germans backed Hitler in 1932 because dynamic rallies contrasted sharply with weak coalitions.
children.gloss: Thirteen million Germans backed Hitler in 1932 because dynamic rallies contrasted sharply with weak coalitions.

children.label: Work of the SA & Street Order
children.gloss: The disciplined work of the SA reinforced Nazi growth by intimidating Communist rivals and running soup kitchens.

children.label: 400,000 SA Paraded Visible Strength
children.detail: Uniformed parades and soup kitchens gave unemployed young men food, purpose, and visible discipline.
children.gloss: Uniformed parades and soup kitchens gave unemployed young men food, purpose, and visible discipline.

children.label: Smashed KPD Red Front Meetings
children.detail: Fierce street battles in Prussia killed scores in summer 1932 while convincing conservatives only Nazis beat Reds.
children.gloss: Fierce street battles in Prussia killed scores in summer 1932 while convincing conservatives only Nazis beat Reds.

children.label: Fear of Communism Drove SA Support
children.detail: Middle-class voters tolerated Brownshirt thuggery mainly because Great Depression chaos threatened Red revolution.
children.gloss: Middle-class voters tolerated Brownshirt thuggery mainly because Great Depression chaos threatened Red revolution.

children.label: Paramilitary Muscle Crushed Rivals
children.detail: Tearing down SPD and KPD posters while dominating town squares actively silenced democratic campaigning.
children.gloss: Tearing down SPD and KPD posters while dominating town squares actively silenced democratic campaigning.

children.label: 2.4 Hitler Becomes Chancellor
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: View 1 argues backstairs intrigue by von Papen and Hindenburg handed power to a fading movement vs View 2 argues leading the largest Reichstag party made Hitler impossible to ignore.

children.label: 1932 Presidential & Reichstag Vote
children.gloss: The Presidential and Reichstag elections of 1932 made the Nazis Germany's largest party before dipping in November.

children.label: 37.3% Peak Blocked Majority Rule
children.detail: Winning 230 seats in July 1932 let Göring as Reichstag Speaker paralyse any cabinet excluding Hitler.
children.gloss: Winning 230 seats in July 1932 let Göring as Reichstag Speaker paralyse any cabinet excluding Hitler.

children.label: Dropped to 196 Seats in November
children.detail: Campaign fatigue and SA brutality cost two million votes, drained party funds, and sparked Strasser's split.
children.gloss: Campaign fatigue and SA brutality cost two million votes, drained party funds, and sparked Strasser's split.

children.label: Nazi Vote Had Already Peaked
children.detail: Falling support and near-bankruptcy in late 1932 meant Hitler could never have seized office without elite help.
children.gloss: Falling support and near-bankruptcy in late 1932 meant Hitler could never have seized office without elite help.

children.label: Still Far Ahead of Every Rival
children.detail: Even at 196 seats, the NSDAP remained larger than the SPD or KPD, starving Papen and Schleicher of majorities.
children.gloss: Even at 196 seats, the NSDAP remained larger than the SPD or KPD, starving Papen and Schleicher of majorities.

children.label: Hindenburg, Papen & Jan 1933
children.gloss: Hitler became Chancellor on 30 January 1933 through the roles of Hindenburg, Kurt von Schleicher, and Franz von Papen.

children.label: Schleicher Failed to Split the Nazis
children.detail: When Strasser backed down in December 1932, Chancellor Schleicher lost both Reichstag and Hindenburg's trust.
children.gloss: When Strasser backed down in December 1932, Chancellor Schleicher lost both Reichstag and Hindenburg's trust.

children.label: Secret Pact at Schröder's Villa
children.detail: Meeting Hitler in January 1933, Papen agreed a coalition cabinet containing just two other Nazi ministers.
children.gloss: Meeting Hitler in January 1933, Papen agreed a coalition cabinet containing just two other Nazi ministers.

children.label: Papen Boasted of Taming Hitler
children.detail: Conservative elites fatally miscalculated that non-Nazi ministers could push Hitler into a harmless corner.
children.gloss: Conservative elites fatally miscalculated that non-Nazi ministers could push Hitler into a harmless corner.

children.label: Mass Movement Forced Elite Hand
children.detail: Bankers and Hindenburg only turned to Hitler on 30 January 1933 because he alone commanded millions of voters.
children.gloss: Bankers and Hindenburg only turned to Hitler on 30 January 1933 because he alone commanded millions of voters.

children.label: KT3: Nazi Dictatorship
children.gloss: Key topic 3: Nazi control and dictatorship, 1933–39 — dismantling democracy in 1933–34, the SS-Gestapo police state, Goebbels' propaganda and Church controls, and pre-war opposition.

children.label: 3.1 Creating a Dictatorship
children.gloss: Q3d Core Debate: View 1 argues pseudo-legal decrees and the Enabling Act built Hitler's dictatorship vs View 2 argues ruthless SA violence and the Night of the Long Knives sealed absolute power.

children.label: Reichstag Fire & Emergency Decree
children.gloss: The Reichstag Fire of 27 February 1933 let Hitler suspend civil liberties and crush Communists before March elections.

children.label: Van der Lubbe Arrested in Flames
children.detail: Blaming Dutch communist Marinus van der Lubbe let Göring claim a nationwide Red uprising had begun.
children.gloss: Blaming Dutch communist Marinus van der Lubbe let Göring claim a nationwide Red uprising had begun.

children.label: 4,000 KPD Leaders Jailed Overnight
children.detail: Hindenburg's 28 February Article 48 decree abolished free speech, press freedom, and trial before arrest.
children.gloss: Hindenburg's 28 February Article 48 decree abolished free speech, press freedom, and trial before arrest.

children.label: Fire Decree Lasted Twelve Years
children.detail: Legal emergency powers signed by Hindenburg gave police permanent authority to detain opponents without charge.
children.gloss: Legal emergency powers signed by Hindenburg gave police permanent authority to detain opponents without charge.

children.label: 50,000 SA Auxiliaries Used Terror
children.detail: Göring armed stormtroopers as official police in Prussia, killing 70 opponents to secure 43.9% in March.
children.gloss: Göring armed stormtroopers as official police in Prussia, killing 70 opponents to secure 43.9% in March.

children.label: Enabling Act, Parties & Unions
children.gloss: The Enabling Act led rapidly to the banning of other parties and trade unions during Gleichschaltung in 1933.

children.label: 444–94 Vote Ended Reichstag Rule
children.detail: Barring 81 KPD deputies and promising Catholic protections won Centre votes on 23 March 1933 for four-year rule.
